entries.name: Kettlebell Turkish Get-Up
entries.reason: A multi-stage movement with roughly seven distinct positions. Any three-frame reduction would omit the transitions that make it what it is.

entries.name: Standing Rope Crunch
entries.reason: Source-bound side-view draft with a spine that curls. Standing with the back to a high pulley and the rope ends held over the shoulders against the upper chest; the hips and legs do not move while the spine curls the trunk forward and down, a pause, and a slower return to standing tall. The hands travel with the upper chest, and the cable runs over the shoulder and only lengthens on the way down.
entries.summary: Standing with your back to a high pulley and the rope at the upper chest, curl the spine to crunch the torso down with the hips still, pause, then return slowly to standing tall.

frames.caption: Attach a rope to a high pulley, stand with your back to the machine and hold the rope ends over the shoulders against the upper chest.
Keeping the hips still, curl the spine to crunch the torso down as far as you can control.
Pause at the bottom. Rope stays at the upper chest.
Return slowly to standing tall.
Curl the spine, hips still.

entries.name: Gorilla Chin/Crunch
entries.reason: Source-bound draft, drawn from a 3D model turned 32 degrees with a magnified hand close-up so the underhand grip slightly wider than the shoulders, the bent knees with level shins at the hang, and the simultaneous pull-up and lower-spine knee crunch all read together: hanging with the centre of mass under the bar and the shins level with the floor, pulling up while curling the pelvis and drawing the knees up (keeping the internal knee angle at or above 60 degrees with the shins clear of the thighs) until the knees reach chest height and the nose is level with the bar, and lowering slowly back to the bent-knee hang.
entries.summary: Hanging with an underhand grip slightly wider than the shoulders and the knees bent so the shins are level with the floor, pull yourself up while drawing the knees up until the knees are at chest height and the nose is level with the bar, then lower slowly.

frames.caption: Hang from a bar with an underhand grip slightly wider than the shoulders and bend the knees so the shins are level with the floor.
Pull yourself up while drawing the knees up toward the chest together.
Finish with the knees at chest height and the nose level with the bar.
Lower slowly to a full hang while returning the knees to the start angle.
Reset in a full hang with the knees bent and the shins level with the floor.

entries.name: Hanging Leg Raise
entries.reason: Source-bound draft, drawn from a 3D model turned 30 degrees with a magnified hand close-up so the overhand grip, the straight arms and straight legs, and the lower-spine pelvic curl all show clearly: hanging with the centre of mass directly under the bar on every tick, curling the pelvis up toward the ribs to raise the straight legs above parallel to the floor, lowering slowly without an unsourced top hold, and holding a dead-still hang between reps.
entries.summary: Hanging from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip and straight arms and legs, curl the pelvis up toward the ribs to raise the legs above parallel to the floor, then lower slowly back to a dead-still hang.

frames.caption: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, arms and legs straight in a dead-still hang.
Begin raising the straight legs while keeping the arms long.
Curl the pelvis up towards the ribs to raise the legs above parallel to the floor.
Begin lowering the straight legs slowly under control.
Complete the slow return back to a dead hang.
Pause in a dead-still hang between repetitions.

entries.name: Kettlebell Turkish Get-Up (Lunge style)
entries.reason: Source-bound draft, drawn from a 3D model turned 24 degrees so the locked-out vertical working arm overhead, the same-side bent knee with its foot planted, the free hand planted on the floor from lying through the push to seated and onto one knee, the knee on the floor while the trunk comes upright, and the stand all read step by step, with whatever bears weight in contact with the floor at every stage (the head segment tilts toward the overhead bell while the unmarked head circle cannot show eye gaze directly): keeping the working arm vertical and locked out from lying to standing and back.
entries.summary: Lying on your back with one kettlebell locked out on a vertical arm and the same-side knee bent, use the free hand to push up to a seated position, then to one knee, stand up from the one-knee position looking up at the bell, and reverse the same sequence back to the floor.

frames.caption: Lie on your back, press the kettlebell to a locked-out arm, and bend the knee on the same side with the foot flat.
Keeping the arm locked out, pivot to the opposite side and use the free hand to drive forward and push up to a seated position.
Keeping the arm locked out, push up from seated onto one knee with the free hand still on the floor.
Looking up at the kettlebell, bring the trunk upright over the knee with the arm locked out.
Looking up at the kettlebell, stand up from the one-knee position.
Reverse the same path back down to one knee with the arm locked out.
Place the free hand back on the floor and lower toward the seated position.
Reverse back to seated on the floor, keeping the arm locked out.
Return to lying on your back with the kettlebell locked out overhead.
